title: Energy: from fossil fuels to windmills
subtitle: oil wells, wind farms, carbon footprint
summary: Name the world's energy sources, from coal mines and offshore drilling platforms to wind farms and geothermal power, and talk about using less energy at home.

lesson.heading: Fossil fuels
lesson.text: **Fossil fuels** are sources of energy which were formed underground from plant and animal remains millions of years ago. An **oil well** is a hole made in the ground for the removal of oil. **Offshore** means away from the coast, so **offshore drilling platforms** explore the ocean bed for oil and gas.

examples.text: Several new **oil wells** were constructed in the desert last year.
Fire has broken out on an **offshore drilling platform**.
A new gas **pipeline** was built to bring cheaper energy to the capital city.
examples.note: pipeline = a very large tube through which liquid or gas flows long distances

lesson.heading: Coal
lesson.text: A **coal mine** is a deep hole, or system of holes, under the ground from which coal is removed. A power station that burns coal is **coal-fired**.

examples.text: Older, **coal-fired** power stations generally cause high levels of pollution.
The **coal mines** in the north of the country are no longer profitable.
The power station is **coal-fired**, but it will soon be replaced by a **nuclear** plant.

lesson.heading: Renewable energy
rows: a group of wind turbines used for producing electricity; onshore means on the land
devices that change energy from the sun into electricity
electricity produced by the force of fast-moving water such as rivers or waterfalls
dead plant and animal material suitable for using as fuel
energy produced by the force of the sea tide
energy produced by the force of waves in the sea
energy from the heat inside the earth
power produced when the nucleus of an atom is divided or joined to another
lesson.note: Renewable energy can be produced again as quickly as it is used. Renewable is also a countable noun: the government will focus on renewables.

lesson.heading: The words in the news
lesson.text: These are the phrases you meet in headlines and reports about energy policy. Note **onshore** for wind farms on land, and its opposite **offshore**.

examples.text: **Onshore wind farms** to get new government subsidies.
**Solar panels** to be installed on all government buildings.
**Tidal power** and **wave power** may meet future energy needs.
**Geothermal** energy will last 1,000 years, says scientist.

lesson.heading: Using less energy at home
lesson.text: **Consumption** is how much of something is used, and to **consume** is to use, especially in large amounts. **Power-hungry** **appliances** - electrical equipment such as washing machines and fridges - use a great deal of energy. You can **monitor** your use of electricity, which means regularly watching and checking it, and choose **energy-efficient** models that use only a little electricity.

examples.text: We're **monitoring** our energy use at home and trying to **consume** less power.
Most recent washing machines and other domestic **appliances** are quite **energy-efficient**.
Switch off entertainment systems that use power while on **standby**.

lesson.heading: Gas-guzzlers, food miles and carbon footprints
lesson.text: A **gas-guzzler** is an informal word for a car that uses a lot of fuel. **Food miles** are the distance food travels from where it is produced to the consumer. Your **carbon footprint** is a measurement of the amount of carbon dioxide your activities create.

examples.text: This car is a real **gas-guzzler**. It has a very high fuel **consumption**.
Think about **food miles** and buy local products.
We can reduce our **carbon footprint** by cutting out unnecessary journeys.

lesson.heading: Finite resources
lesson.text: The world's coal, oil and gas **deposits** - layers formed under the ground over a very long period - are **finite**: they have an end, and one day they will **run out**.

examples.text: The planet only contains a **finite** amount of oil and coal.

lesson.text: Take care with the spelling of energy - not ~~energie~~ or ~~energi~~.

exercises.prompt: Match each energy word with its description.

pairs.right: a very large tube carrying gas or oil long distances
a structure out at sea exploring the ocean bed for oil
devices that turn the heat of the sun into electricity
a deep hole under the ground from which coal is removed
a group of turbines producing electricity
dead plant and animal material used as fuel

exercises.prompt: A new 100-kilometre ___ has been built to bring oil from the wells to a refinery on the coast.
exercises.explanation: A pipeline is a very large tube through which liquid or gas can flow for long distances.

exercises.prompt: The power station is ___ , but it will soon be replaced by a nuclear plant.
exercises.explanation: A coal-fired power station uses coal as a fuel.

exercises.prompt: Fire has broken out on an ___ drilling platform.
exercises.explanation: Offshore means away from or at a distance from the coast; onshore means on the land.

exercises.prompt: Some parts of the world may be able to use ___ energy, which comes from the heat inside the earth.
exercises.explanation: Geothermal energy uses the heat inside the earth.

exercises.prompt: We should consider the issue of ___ when shopping for fruit and vegetables and try to buy local produce.
exercises.hint: (two words: how far food has travelled)
exercises.explanation: Food miles are the distance food is transported from where it is produced to the consumer.

exercises.prompt: Most recent models of washing machines use less power than older ones and are quite ___ .
exercises.explanation: An energy-efficient appliance uses only a little electricity or gas.

exercises.prompt: The company is trying to reduce its ___ by allowing fewer foreign trips and using video-conferencing.
exercises.hint: (two words: the carbon dioxide your activities create)
exercises.explanation: Your carbon footprint measures the amount of carbon dioxide your activities create.

exercises.prompt: This car is a real ___ . It has a very high fuel consumption.
exercises.hint: (informal, hyphenated: uses a lot of fuel)
exercises.explanation: A gas-guzzler is an informal word for a car that uses a lot of fuel.

exercises.prompt: The planet only contains a ___ amount of oil and coal. One day the deposits will run out.
exercises.explanation: Finite means having an end or lasting a limited time.

exercises.prompt: 'The country is developing two main energy sources: ___ and hydroelectric power stations.' Which word fits?
exercises.explanation: Biomass is dead plant and animal material used as fuel.

exercises.statement: An onshore wind farm is built out at sea.
exercises.explanation: Onshore means on the land; a wind farm out at sea is an offshore wind farm.

exercises.prompt: Is each one a fossil fuel source or a renewable one?
